title: Unit & Style Constraint Workshop: Code Transformation Scenarios
content:
Overview:

This working doc collects a compact, practical corpus of transformation scenarios we will use for model onboarding and regression checks when evaluating code generation and automated refactoring behaviors. The emphasis is on end-to-end correctness signals: the model's output should compile (where applicable), pass a small unit harness, and respect style constraints or transformation invariants. This is a workshop-style artifact — intentionally pragmatic and iterative.

Goals:
- Provide a lightweight but diverse set of prompts and target checks that capture common real-world developer tasks: add a failing unit test, implement a small feature, refactor for readability, or apply a style rule.
- Encourage deterministic pass/fail signals that can be automated in the CI harness (compile exit codes, unit test results, linters).
- Surface subtle failure modes: partial implementations, wrong function signatures, broken imports, off-by-one loops, and regressions to previously working prompts.

Scope and constraints:
- Languages: initial focus on Python and Go (most on Python).
- Scenario types: implement-from-spec, repair-to-pass, API-stub-to-impl, extraction/refactor preserving behaviour, and style-normalization transformations.
- Each scenario includes: a short prompt, minimal starting repository state, a ground-truth or oracle test harness, and explicit acceptance criteria.
- Keep corpus small and fast: per-case CI runtime target <= 30s on our ephemeral test runner.

Dataset composition (high level):
- 28 scenarios total (16 Python, 8 Go, 4 cross-language).
- Categories: compilation-only (6), unit-harness (12), style-gate (6), mixed (4).
- Complexity bins: tiny (single-file <20 LOC): 12, small multi-file (20-200 LOC): 10, interdependent (200+ LOC or package-level): 6.

Example scenarios (representative samples):
1) "sum-range" (tiny, Python, compilation + unit): Implement function sum_range(a, b) where b may be less than a (return 0). Tests include edge cases for negative numbers and swapped bounds. Acceptance: python -m pytest returns 0.

2) "normalize-paths" (small, Go, compilation + unit): Given a package that manipulates filesystem paths, implement NormalizePath to consistently handle trailing slashes and OS separators. Acceptance: go test passes and go vet shows no issues.

3) "fix-off-by-one" (tiny, Python, unit): Given failing test demonstrating off-by-one error in pagination function, modify code to pass tests without changing public API. Acceptance: tests pass, no new flaky markers.

4) "style-rename-vars" (style-gate, Python): Reformat variable names to snake_case and ensure black/flake8 are clean. Acceptance: black --check exits 0 and flake8 exit 0 for the modified files.

5) "extract-logger" (refactor, Python, mixed): Extract a logging helper to a new module and update imports; behavior must remain identical (monkeypatched log sink should receive same messages during tests). Acceptance: unit harness compares log capture output before/after.

6) "api-contract-change" (interdependent, cross-language): Small change in an interface (add optional parameter) and ensure wrapper code in Go and client in Python still interoperate. Acceptance: integration smoke tests succeed.

Prompt engineering patterns (how prompts are authored for this corpus):
- Minimal context: provide the small repo snapshot as code blocks and a short task description. Avoid long expository text that confuses token budgets.
- Explicit constraints: state "do not modify test files" or "preserve function signature" where necessary.
- Example-driven: include 1–2 input/output examples for ambiguous tasks (e.g., normalization rules).
- Negative guards: call out what not to do when models tend to over-optimize (e.g., avoid dropping error returns in Go).

Evaluation metrics and acceptance rules (automatable signals):
- Primary pass/fail: exit code of test harness (0 == pass).
- Secondary checks: linter status (black/flake8/go vet), static analyzers (mypy), and compile status.
- Quality signals: number of changed lines (delta), new TODOs introduced, and presence of brittle patterns (eval via simple regex heuristics).
- Performance: wall-time for the end-to-end run (target <30s per scenario).
- Flakiness detection: run failing cases 3x to detect nondeterministic passes.

Harness integration notes (CI):
- Each scenario is stored as a small fixture directory. Our harness will: checkout fixture, run the model with a preconfigured endpoint, apply patch file (or write returned files), then run the scenario script which runs compile/lint/tests and returns a structured result.
- Use isolated ephemeral containers. Avoid network access in harness.
- For large-model runs, include a canonical seed/environment to minimize output variability (prompt temperature 0.0 where possible, and include explicit "deterministic" instruction).

Pass/fail policy examples (explicit):
- Compilation-only: pass if compiler returns exit code 0 for main target and no new warnings flagged as errors.
- Unit-harness: pass if all tests in harness succeed and no modifications were made to test files.
- Style-gate: pass if stylistic tools return success and code changes are limited to allowed files.
- Mixed: must satisfy all applicable checks. If tests fail but linter is fine, outcome = FAIL.

Known pitfalls and anti-patterns we've seen in earlier onboarding attempts:
- Model truncates patches or returns diff with context lines that the patch tool can't apply. Fix: canonicalize patch format or include trimmed edit-only suggestions.
- Overly clever renames that break public API. Fix: include invariant text in prompt requiring preserved signatures.
- Missing imports: common in generated code. Fix: detect via static import checker and heuristically add missing imports before running tests (but count as a model penalty).

Scheduling, regression cadence, and ownership:
- Short-term: add 8 highest-value scenarios to onboarding CI as smoke. (Owner: Maya Patel).
- Medium-term (quarter): expand to full 28-case corpus and add flakiness detection. (Owner: eng-applied-ml).
- Regression policy: any model rollout that reduces pass-rate on the smoke set by >3% requires hold and manual review.

Next steps & action items (workshop outcomes):
- [ ] Convert the 8 smoke scenarios into fixture directories and push to repo: github.com/redwood-inference/evals-fixtures (owner: Liam).
- [ ] Implement CI harness hook that can apply model-produced patches reliably (owner: Sofia).
- [ ] Draft a short onboarding README for model teams with prompt templates and examples (owner: Maya).
- [ ] Run a dry-run with current staging model and collect failure modes (owner: Ethan).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally concise and operational. Expect edits — particularly around pass criteria and the specific examples used. Please add scenario ideas as short bullets in the doc comments below rather than long rewrites.

Appendix: short example prompt (canonicalized)
"""
Repo snapshot: files:
- utils/math_ops.py (contains TODO)
- tests/test_math_ops.py (failing tests)
Task: implement sum_range(a, b) in utils/math_ops.py. Do not change tests. Keep function signature exactly as is. Return an integer. Edge behavior: if b < a return 0.
Constraints: code must be idiomatic Python 3.11, pass black and flake8.
Expected signal: python -m pytest exits 0 and black --check passes.
"""

-- end of working draft --
